name: NAPW Canadian Heritage Championship
notes: A "NAPW Heritage Championship" is also named once in the classic-era served corpus (Stone Zellor, Anniversary Assault II, 31 Oct 2007); whether it shares a lineage with this belt is unresolved.
epitaph: The revived era's own third championship, restarted vacant in a May 2014 five-way melee that Sammy Devine won. Changed hands between Devine and Bruiser Breton twice across the Phenomenons' own touring season, then again to a name the fed's own title-history ledger never recorded a transition for — the ledger's own last word (28 Dec 2014, Devine) and the 2014 Year End Awards' own later snapshot (Feb 2015, Prince Wadjethotep) simply disagree, a gap in the surviving record, not a resolved handoff.

name: NAPW Provincial Championship
epitaph: NAPW's own second singles title, crowned the same debut night as the World Championship — Ravager beat "The Moose" Mark Millar for it, 31 Oct 2005 — and changed hands repeatedly through the classic era's own first two years.

name: NAPW Television Championship
notes: Reigns here are a partial reconstruction from title-change callouts across the served show corpus, not a single ledger.
epitaph: A classic-era-only mid-card title (2005-2010), never revived after the 2010 closure as far as the surviving record shows. "Dirty" Don Travelli held it across at least two separate reigns per the served corpus, trading it with Lobo; the fed's own Sept 2010 rankings sidebar confirms Chris Casino as champion at the classic era's own close, though the hand-off from Travelli's own last confirmed reign (Apr 2006) isn't in the held corpus — years of real, unreconstructed gap.

name: NAPW World Championship
epitaph: NAPW's own top title from its first night on — The Plague won it in a match at the very debut show, 31 Oct 2005 — through a densely-chained run of classic-era champions (Patrick Bickle, "Perfection" Evan Cartwright, and two Ravager reigns, the second a ten-defense run ended by Donovan Astros on a date the fed's own broadcast called live, 31 Jul 2007) into an overseas ECFW/REBEL tour and a three-plus-year Astros reign confirmed still standing by the fed's own Sept 2010 rankings, the classic era's own last word. Into the promotion's 2010 closure and 2013 revival, the title restarted vacant and ran through five more champions — Anton Petrov, Clancy King, Abbey Graves, Jay Deschain, and Declan Black, the revived era's own last-recorded champion — a chain the fed's own title-history ledger keeps complete from Nov 2013 on. One real, named gap remains in the classic-era chain: exactly when and to whom Ravager first lost the title, sometime between his Feb 2006 win and Bickle's Oct 2006 win, isn't in the held record.

name: World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: The revived era's own tag belt, carrying a four-month reign by the touring outside act the Phenomenons — a four-way at Tagstravaganza to Flavour Explosion — before Those That Would Inflict Ill took it over and were still champions as of the January 2015 roster snapshot the record ends on.

name: NAPW Pure Honor Championship
epitaph: A classic-era NAPW belt contested on technical-wrestling terms — its own roster bios name holders and contenders, though no dated lineage survives in the recovered record.

name: NAPW Extreme Jobber Championship
epitaph: NAPW's own joke belt played straight — an Extreme Jobber Championship whose first holder, "Bad Boy" Joey Malone, is credited by his own bio card, which also records him losing the honor to Nightmare.
